title: heuristic DAG runbook compiler and local repro hints
author: Evelyn Chen
release_notes: Introduces a DAG-based runbook compiler that emits compact conditional playbooks and localized repro hints; includes a small local repro runner for oncall use. Backwards compatible with existing playbook format.
description: Motivation: Oncall responders frequently need a concise, executable set of steps that adapt to observed telemetry. This PR introduces a heuristic DAG compiler that converts high-level runbook templates and telemetry predicates into compact conditional playbooks plus short local repro hints (minimal traces, query snippets, and service call stubs). Design: 1) A lightweight DAG IR captures nodes (check, query, mitigation, escalate) and edges with guard predicates; 2) Compiler heuristics prune nodes unlikely to apply given recent telemetry (configurable thresholds) and collapse linear chains into single composite actions to reduce cognitive load; 3) Local repro hint extractor synthesizes a minimal set of queries/trace spans and a docker-compose sandbox recipe (when available) to reproduce the symptom locally; 4) Safe-mode runner executes a dry-run passing through the DAG with simulated telemetry to validate branch coverage. Checklist: - added DAG IR and in-memory evaluator; - implemented three pruning heuristics (frequency, recency, impact score); - added repro-hint extractor with sanitizers and redaction rules; - added unit tests for compiler, evaluator, and sanitizer; - added integration test that runs compiler on 20 existing runbooks and compares size reduction and coverage; - added small CLI `slo runbook-compile --input ... --dry-run` and a `slo runbook-local-repro` helper; - documented new config knobs in docs/runbooks/README.md; - feature gated behind feature flag `runbook_dag_compiler` and rollout plan in this PR. Testing & rollout: Unit tests pass locally and in CI. Integration runs showed a median runbook size reduction of 42% for the sampled corpus while preserving coverage for configured test prompts. Canary rollout: enabled for a 5% oncall group for two weeks, monitor false-positive rate and responder feedback. Migration: existing runbooks are still usable; CLI and API will accept both legacy and DAG format for 3 months before deprecating legacy authoring path. Safety and security: repro hints are sanitized using the project's redaction policy; any hint that would include PII or secrets is replaced with placeholders and an automated review flag is raised. Impact: intended to speed triage and lower MTTR by delivering more focused instructions and an ability to run quick local replays.
